result.title: DeltaTTT: Layerwise Optimization for Nonlinear Recurrent Memory
result.summary: Sequential test-time training adapts a memory network through successive updates, each computing an inner-loop gradient based on the network's previous state. Intuitively, this state dependence should allow each update to account for what the memory has already learned and better incorporate new information. However, we find that this expected advantage does not consistently materialize in nonlinear memories: a fixed-base parallel TTT baseline outperforms its serial counterpart. Our exploratory experiments point to a key underlying difficulty: nonlinear memories can be harder to optimize than linear ones within a single pass over the sequence. To alleviate this optimization difficulty, we introduce DeltaTTT, which replaces joint inner-loop optimization of a two-layer memory network with layerwise learning. Each layer is assigned a local prediction target and updated through a state-dependent delta rule. This formulation retains a nonlinear readout while enabling chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on DeltaNet and LaCT backbones show improvements in language modeling and retrieval over their recurrent baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究非线性循环记忆的序列测试时训练，发现固定基底的并行 TTT 反而优于串行版本，并将两层记忆网络的联合内循环优化改为逐层学习、每层用状态相关的 delta 规则更新，从而在保持非线性读出下支持分块并行计算。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 latent memory 工作，但其「状态相关更新 + 逐层优化 + chunk 并行」线索可能为 LVR 的 latent 状态更新与贡献分配提供可核查的方法借鉴，值得近读。
